Joaquín Sánchez Desalojo de la playa de El Trampolín, este jueves. Joaquín Sánchez Los agentes desplazan y tratan de convencer a los migrantes para que se dirijan hacia los centros habilitados este jueves por el Gobierno. Joaquín Sánchez Llegada de efectivos de la Guardia Civil y del Ejército a la playa de El Trampolín, este jueves. Joaquín Sánchez

La playa ha sido desalojada por razones humanitarias, según fuentes del dispositivo. Los primeros grupos, y más numerosos, han dejado la playa a las 9.46 con gritos de júbilo, gestos de triunfo y saludando a los periodistas y policías del dispositivo de seguridad. Las tiendas construidas en la playa con cartones y ramas se han quedado prácticamente vacías, en la zona quedaban algunos rezagados, menos de media docena, a los que los agentes de Guardia Civil instaban a marcharse porque se iba a limpiar todo. Las brigadas de limpieza han podido desmantelar una parte del poblado, pero cuando la presencia policial se ha retirado, han regresado varios grupos de migrantes que están durmiendo en una zona de monte cercana para rebuscar e intentar aprovechar algunos de los objetos que se habían quedado abandonados.

En torno a las dos de la tarde, el Gobierno ceutí ha señalado que se ha visto obligado a pausar la limpieza de la playa por el regreso de “alrededor de 500 personas” con el pretexto de recoger o buscar pertenencias personales. Estos migrantes, la mayoría marroquíes, se han terminado quedando en la zona.

El grupo de migrantes más numeroso ha ido caminando hasta Loma Margarita. Tras subir la cuesta de Caballería, una vía de comunicación que discurre junto al Cuartel Coronel Galindo y la pista de atletismo, han llegado a un recinto militar que se solía utilizar para hacer prácticas de autoescuela. Los migrantes se han cobijado bajo tres estructuras metálicas paralelas pintadas de color verde, similares a una nave, pero sin las paredes laterales. Dos agentes de policía custodiaban la entrada y no permitían que nadie accediera. A través de la puerta se les veía sentados primero y formando filas después. Estaban esperando su turno para hacer un prerregistro con el que comenzarán a recabar información de cada uno de los casos y que les proporcionará un número o una referencia.

Los marroquíes desalojados de El Trampolín estaban un poco más recelosos sobre su nuevo destino. Los agentes han reubicado a un grupo en el aparcamiento de la llamada zona del Embolsamiento, en Loma Colmenar, donde aguardaban a que les dieran instrucciones sentados en el suelo. Alrededor del lugar, al que tampoco se podía acceder de forma libre, pululaban decenas de compatriotas que observaban lo que ocurría y a los que los agentes han pastoreado monte arriba hacia el barrio de El Príncipe. “No nos dejan pasar. Nos dicen que ahora no”, contaban. Los que estaban fuera no ocultaban su recelo porque ese aparcamiento es el paso previo a cruzar la frontera hacia Marruecos y se utiliza especialmente durante la Operación Paso del Estrecho. Tanto los agentes del dispositivo de seguridad como los trabajadores de las entidades que les atienden les han negado que fueran a expulsarles, sino que se trataba de darles cobijo y mejorar sus condiciones.

Vista del espacio de Loma Margarita, este jueves. Joaquín Sánchez

Los espacios se han acondicionado con catres (literas), mesas para comer y aseos, según fuentes del Ministerio de Inclusión y Migraciones. Allí podrán encontrar agua y atención psicosocial, añaden.

Desde la puerta del centro de Loma Margarita, cerca de la Playa de El Trampolín, no se alcanzaba a ver las camas en las que dormirán este jueves, mientras que en la zona de Loma Colmenar, cerca de la frontera, sí que había varias decenas de tiendas de campaña militares. A algunas se les había volado parte de la tela por el viento que sopló la noche del miércoles y estaban recomponiéndolas.

“Esto va a continuar en los próximos días”, avanzaba la ministra de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones, que también advertía de que se trata de un trabajo “delicado” que pone en el centro lo humanitario y que también persigue que la ciudad autónoma vaya recuperando la normalidad.

World.title: Adiós lavanda, hola girasoles: un viaje por Burgos cuando en agosto cambia de color
World.content:
Cuando los tonos morados desaparecen de los campos, el amarillo toma el relevo en la comarca de La Bureba o la Ribera del Duero, con Briviesca, Poza de la Sal y Caleruega como paradas principales para descubrir el patrimonio burgalés

En agosto, Burgos cambia el perfume por la luz. Al recorrer los campos de la provincia por carreteras secundarias y caminos, el viajero aprecia una muda de color: la lavanda que en julio pinta hectáreas de morado deja paso a los girasoles, que colorean de amarillo vastas extensiones de La Bureba y algunos paisajes de la Ribera del Duero.

Quien quiera rodearse de miles de girasoles —esas flores que Van Gogh volvió universales— debe acudir durante esta época del año a La Bureba. Allí los girasoles aparecen a los lados de las carreteras, y se convierten en uno de los grandes protagonistas del paisaje durante unas semanas. Caminar junto a los campos en su momento más vigoroso puede justificar por sí solo la visita a esta comarca y sus pueblos.

Más información Begur: el pueblo de Girona en el que se para el reloj

El mejor punto de partida para entender el paisaje estival de esta comarca burgalesa, que, además, fue de las primeras en adquirir personalidad dentro del condado castellano, es la localidad de Briviesca. En esta época del año los girasoles se muestran en su máximo esplendor y embellecen aún más al pueblo. Briviesca invita a detenerse y mirar los campos más allá de su condición de cultivo. La iniciativa Girasoles con Arte, puesta en marcha en 2024, combina el patrimonio urbano de Briviesca y el paisaje agrícola mediante dos trazados sencillos: uno de 1,63 kilómetros y otro de 2,67 kilómetros.

La plaza Mayor de Briviesca, en la provincia de Burgos. Teo Moreno Moreno (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Quienes deseen conocer más a fondo el ambiente local en torno a los girasoles pueden combinar paseos junto a ese paisaje efímero con una visita más detenida por el pueblo. La propuesta puede realizarse en medio día, y se puede iniciar con una etapa más urbana. Esta se desarrolla a lo largo de distintos puntos de interés de la localidad conocida como La Bien Trazada, por su plano ortogonal con forma de tablero de ajedrez. Comienza en la plaza Mayor, el punto desde el que la localidad muestra su trazado rectilíneo. En el centro se levanta un templete musical de estilo modernista construido en 1909. La siguiente parada está a escasos metros, en la excolegiata de Santa María la Mayor, iniciada en el siglo XIV y reformada en el siglo XVIII. La ruta continúa hacia el monasterio de Santa Clara, cuyo interior alberga un retablo de más de 20 metros de altura, tallado en madera de nogal y singular por carecer de policromía. La ausencia de color permite apreciar la minuciosidad de la talla, que bajo una capa de policromía podría haberse relegado a un segundo plano. Esa falta de acabado, atribuida a problemas económicos, terminó por convertirse en una de sus particularidades más reconocibles.

Retablo mayor en la nave central de la Iglesia de Santa Clara. Miguel Sotomayor (GETTY IMAGES)

Pero el encanto del girasol en La Bureba no se queda solo en Briviesca. El viaje continúa hacia Poza de la Sal, un recorrido que lleva al viajero a través de extensas hectáreas doradas cercanas a los pueblos de Quintanabureba y Llano de Bureba. En Poza de la Sal, el amarillo del verano encuentra un contrapunto mineral e histórico: una villa encaramada al borde de la llanura, con el castillo de los Rojas en lo alto y las antiguas salinas hundidas en el diapiro que dio nombre al pueblo. Conocida también como el Balcón de la Bureba, permite una vista amplia sobre la llanura de la comarca antes de volver a la carretera.

Un campo de girasoles cerca de Poza de la Sal. Architect´s Eye / Alamy / Cordon PRess

Al sur de la provincia, el amarillo cambia de compañía. Mientras que en La Bureba crece junto a cereales y llanuras, en la Ribera florece entre viñas y el recuerdo reciente de la lavanda. Después de la siega, la lavanda permanece en aceites esenciales, aguas florales, jabones, perfumes y otros productos elaborados en la zona. Así, Caleruega y Cilleruelo de Arriba han empezado a construir en el sur burgalés una pequeña cultura alrededor de esta planta.

Una calle en la localidad burgalesa de Poza de la Sal. Jose Luis Alvarez Esteban (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Quien se acerque a Caleruega para seguir el rastro dorado en los terrenos que circundan al pueblo entrará también en un lugar que no se entiende sin su más ilustre personaje: Santo Domingo de Guzmán, patrón provincial. Al llegar al casco urbano, el Torreón de los Guzmanes se yergue con 17 metros de altura desde época medieval sobre el resto de la arquitectura local. Le acompaña el Real Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, fundado en 1266 por mandato del rey Alfonso X el Sabio, que en su interior alberga un claustro gótico y el Pocito de Santo Domingo, donde la tradición sitúa el nacimiento del santo y al que se atribuyen propiedades milagrosas. En lo alto del casco urbano, la iglesia de San Sebastián, de piedra románica, vigila la plaza mayor del pueblo desde el siglo XII. De esta parroquia procede la pila donde fue bautizado Santo Domingo, trasladada fuera de Caleruega y utilizada en bautizos de miembros de la Casa Real española desde 1605.

El claustro del Real Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, en la localidad de Caleruega. Blanca Saenz de Castillo (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Quien quiera detenerse más tiempo en la zona encontrará, además de los campos de girasoles que acompañan algunas carreteras de acceso, otros puntos de interés. El Sendero de las Loberas, de 10,2 kilómetros, permite acercarse a esas construcciones circulares de piedra que servían para resguardar el ganado de los lobos. En el entorno de Caleruega también aparecen otros vestigios, como los yacimientos arqueológicos de San Mamés y La Pudia o la Bodega de Alfonso VIII, vinculada al despoblado de San Martín de Bañuelos.

La ruta en busca de más hectáreas doradas por el sur de Burgos puede prolongarse por la Ribera hacia el pueblo vecino de Baños de Valdearados. Allí, la Villa Romana de Santa Cruz recuerda la huella de Roma en el territorio, mientras que a finales de agosto la fiesta en honor a Baco, dios romano del vino, llena el pueblo de togas, desfiles, mercado y vino de la Ribera (este año se celebra el 22 y 23 de agosto).

Celebración de la Fiesta a Baco, en Baños de Valdearados. Carlos Mora (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Otra parada cercana es Villanueva de Gumiel, que permite prolongar esa continuación amarilla del verano por los campos de la Ribera. En sus calles se aprecian las fachadas de las casas antiguas, con una arquitectura caracterizada por plantas bajas de mampostería de piedra y plantas altas de entramado de madera y adobe. La iglesia de San Mamés, del siglo XVII, se diferencia de otras formas tradicionales al estructurarse en dos naves simétricas con ocho arcos cruzados y un valioso retablo del siglo XVI.

Recorrer con calma estos pueblos burgaleses permite disfrutar de un manto dorado que parece no agotarse desde la carretera. En estas tierras, la floración suele regalar sus mejores imágenes entre finales de julio y agosto. Y a quienes busquen mejores fotos suele convenirles acercarse al amanecer, momento en el que los rayos de sol iluminan de frente las cabezas maduras que miran hacia el este.

Como en toda floración agrícola, el estado de cada parcela cambia según la siembra, el calor y el momento de cosecha, por lo que conviene consultar con las oficinas de turismo antes de emprender la ruta. Y, sobre todo, conviene recordar algo crucial: estos campos no existen para la foto, son cultivos en activo. Hay que respetar todas las flores para que el siguiente visitante pueda admirar los campos de esta Castilla con la misma belleza.

World.title: Begur: el pueblo de Girona en el que se para el reloj
World.content:
Este enclave del Baix Empordà ha logrado conservar la magia de sus playas y calas, goza de algunas de las mejores propuestas culinarias del territorio y atrae por igual a locales y foráneos, permaneciendo en un ventajoso segundo plano a la hora de atraer al turismo masivo

Begur es una localidad catalana cuya fundación los historiadores acostumbran a situar en 1019, con la construcción del castillo de la localidad, aunque sus inicios datan de la época feudal. Ubicada a apenas 30 kilómetros de Girona, esta joya del Baix Empordà consigue permanecer alejada durante gran parte del año de las rutas turísticas masificadas que recorren parajes como Barcelona, la siempre bulliciosa Costa Brava o ciertas zonas del Empordà. Conserva además intacta su capacidad para sorprender al viajero y acumula un buen número de razones que obligan al habitual a seguir volviendo a su calma chicha. En verano la cosa cambia y la población, de apenas 4.000 habitantes, se multiplica por diez, pero, aun así, el pueblo se las ingenia para seguir siendo (relativamente) tranquilo.

Sa Punta, un establecimiento familiar totalmente remodelado de la mano de un grupo de empresarios encabezados por Daniela McLean —ideóloga del proyecto y con amplia experiencia en leyendas de la hostelería de lujo como el Palace Hôtel de Crillon, en París, o el grupo Peninsula Hotels—, se ha convertido en uno de los grandes imanes de esta localidad de cielos limpios y carácter familiar, con su apariencia de casa señorial en cuyo interior se esconde el espíritu de una beach house pensada para apagar el móvil, desenchufar el ordenador y vivir como si el mundo exterior hubiera decidido dejarnos en paz durante unos días.

Más información 16 pueblos españoles que piden manga larga cuando cae la tarde

El jardín del hotel Sa Punta, en Begur.

Este hotel cuenta con 36 habitaciones, un spa, un restaurante con vocación transversal y sin delirios de grandeza (hay arroces, pero también hamburguesas), una piscina perfecta para los que desean ponerse en remojo en lugar de encaminarse hacia la playa y un entorno donde predomina el verde y una tranquilidad casi desconcertante, teniendo en cuenta los desquiciantes parámetros urbanitas. “Estamos en un lugar emblemático, rodeado de campos, de viñedos y de rutas ideales para darse una vuelta en bici o un buen paseo. Es un hotel muy tranquilo porque hacemos yoga y es solo para adultos. Siempre digo que es un hotel que transmite calma: pensado para desconectar totalmente del estrés. Por eso muchas veces insistimos en lo de la beach house para explicar por qué esto no es un hotel de lujo al uso ni un cuatro estrellas convencional”, explica Sandra Julià, la directora del establecimiento. “Tampoco estamos en primera línea de mar, aunque en cinco minutos puedas plantarte en la playa. Es una zona más elevada, así que tenemos unas vistas preciosas, pero con un ambiente mucho más íntimo”, añade sobre este establecimiento que abre de abril a octubre para adaptarse a las necesidades y deseos de su clientela.

La dificultad de acceder a Begur si uno no dispone de coche (el transporte público funciona en la temporada estival, pero sigue siendo complejo acceder al pueblo) se ha convertido, paradójicamente, en una de las ventajas de la localidad. “Totalmente. Lo cierto es que la gran mayoría de nuestros clientes necesitan coche para llegar hasta aquí y está claro que, si fuera accesible con el tren, el autobús y el transporte público, sería muy diferente. Y no solo para el hotel, para toda la zona. La movilidad aquí ya es complicada. Es cierto que a Begur y a Pals puedes llegar en autobús, pero no llega el tren. Eso hace que sea un destino un poco más exclusivo”, confirma Julià.

Vista del castillo de Begur. BORIS STROUJKO (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Más allá de las virtudes de un alojamiento pensado para el reposo y la desconexión, si uno decide salir de Sa Punta, Begur ofrece una triada insuperable: gastronomía, paseos y un sinfín de destellos del pasado. “Creo que eso es precisamente lo que la gente viene buscando. Pueblos medievales como Pals o Peratallada, lugares históricos, una gastronomía increíble, el arroz de Pals y unas playas preciosas. Todas esas pequeñas calas llenas de encanto”, aporta Julià. Pero a pesar del innegable atractivo de la geografía y la idiosincrasia que recorre cada rincón del Baix Empordà, Julià reconoce que algunos de sus clientes vienen buscando cosas distintas: “Por supuesto, hay de todo y también nos gusta que sea así, tener muchos perfiles distintos y ser capaces de atenderles con la misma solvencia. Hay clientes que vienen únicamente a jugar al golf. Comen aquí todos los días y no quieren hacer nada más. O los ciclistas, que pasan el día entero sobre la bicicleta. ¡Hay de todo!”, sonríe.

Para que no queden dudas, la directora de Sa Punta deja claro que en el hotel se prioriza un enfoque centrado en el adulto. El establecimiento es un gran reclamo para el turista familiar, pero solo con adolescentes, ya que la edad mínima son 12 años. “Por eso tenemos muchas parejas o grupos de amigos que vienen a darse un homenaje culinario, y no hay niños, pero pueden traerse a sus perros… siempre que no pesen más de nueve kilos”, aclara.

El bar exterior del hotel Sa Punta.

Para ponerse las botas

Lo del buen comer es casi una obligación para cualquiera que visite este enclave gerundense. La oferta es amplia, el producto impecable y hay un buen número de lugares que parecen sacados de una de esas películas románticas en las que los protagonistas se ponen las botas con el mar de fondo. AlKostat del Mar (en el hotel Finca Victoria) es uno de esos paraísos: con un coloso como el chef Jordi Vilà, responsable de los fogones de dos templos barceloneses como el Alkimia y Alkostat al mando del establecimiento, esta se ha convertido en una de las citas imprescindibles para los amantes de la buena mesa.

El chef Jordi Vilà está al frente de AlKostat del Mar, en el hotel Finca Victoria.

“AlKostat del Mar es un proyecto que puede adaptarse al territorio y es totalmente permeable a la cocina local. Casi podríamos decir que por sedimentación se acomoda allí donde llega. Creo que hacemos una cocina muy fresca, muy de olores, muy de sabores, sencilla: catalana y tradicional, pero siempre con nuestro toque. Como trabajamos mucho con el producto de temporada, pues hay mucho tomate y mucho pescado a la brasa”, explica Vilà. ¿Un plato imprescindible? “La ensaladilla rusa a la brasa, en la que cada ingrediente pasa por las brasas antes de volver al plato. Creo que explica muy bien lo que hacemos”.

Por supuesto, la competencia es feroz y en la lista de los favoritos de la localidad también sacan la cabeza tótems como Cap Sa Sal y la sidrería Mooma. Si hay ganas de aventura, Far Nomo, en Llafranc, es otra recomendación de primera clase y localidades como Peratallada, Pals y Calella de Palafrugell también ofrecen una gran variedad de mesas en las que ponerse las botas.

Para los amantes de los paseos o las calas, Begur es un seguro de vida: en el camino que lleva de Aiguablava a Platja Fonda puede recorrerse uno de los tramos más bellos del Camí de Ronda de la Costa Brava. El sendero transcurre entre pinos y acantilados, enlazando pequeñas calas y miradores naturales con vistas al Mediterráneo. El recorrido culmina en la mencionada Platja Fonda, una playa de arena oscura encajada entre altas paredes rocosas que sigue conservando una atmósfera casi mágica.

Si uno se queda con ganas de más, nada mejor que apostar por la ruta que lleva desde Cap de Begur a El Semàfor, un recorrido menos conocido que permite adentrarse en una de las zonas más agrestes del litoral de Begur. Un sendero que llega a una antigua estación electro-semafórica (la mencionada, El Semàfor), inaugurada en 1891 para orientar a los barcos de la Costa Brava. En el extremo del Cap de Begur, el edificio se abre hoy como mirador privilegiado sobre el mar.

Con tanto paseo, piscina, bici, golf y banquete, puede que en algún momento apetezca la irremediable tentación del dulce: para eso existe la Pastisseria Pa de pessic, uno de esos sitios a los que hay que ir dispuesto a dejarse aconsejar. “Abrí hace unos seis años y aposté desde el principio por la pastelería tradicional, pero reduciendo un 20% el azúcar. Abro todo el año y, aparte de brazos de gitano, coronas y pasteles como el de requesón (con queso local) o tiramisú con ratafía, mi producto estrella es el buñuelo del Empordà”, cuenta Anna Ferret, que regenta este palacete del dulce en la localidad gerundense.

Uno de los rulos de nata de la la Pastisseria Pa de pessic, en Begur.

La directora de Sa Punta quiere ofrecer a los interesados un último aliciente: “Tenemos un plus, que es algo que a mí me gusta mucho, y es que existe un gran sentimiento de comunidad que a su vez se traduce en una gran dosis de solidaridad: Sa punta forma parte de Costa Brava Centre y yo conozco a la mayoría de los directores de hoteles cercanos. Si tengo un banquete y me faltan sesenta platos, se los pido al hotel de al lado. Siempre nos ayudamos y eso me parece extraordinario en los tiempos que corren”. “Supongo que también es un buen modo de resumir lo que es Begur: un lugar en el que nunca te faltará de nada”, remata Julià.

World.title: Bruls calls on justice ministry to enforce motorway tractor ban
World.content:
Local politicians have called for nationwide rules to be enforced to keep tractors off motorways in the wake of a fatal crash during a farmers’ protest a week ago.

Hubert Bruls, mayor of Nijmegen and chair of the board of regional safety councils, said it was “incomprehensible” that local authorities took different approaches to enforcing the traffic rules.

Last Friday two people died in a collision on the A59 at the tail end of a queue that had built up on the A59 near Hees, a suburb of Nijmegen.

Police and the prosecution service had said before the collision happened that they would not prosecute farmers who drove tractors onto the motorway, even though they are prohibited, citing the right to demonstrate.

The prosecution service has since said that anyone who drives a tractor onto the motorway will be subject to enforcement, even though police said at an earlier demonstration that they did not have enough evidence to go on because the farmers had taped over their numberplates.

Bruls told NOS he wanted to hold talks with the justice ministry to decide on a national strategy for offences on the motorway.

“It’s not manageable for the police if every mayor comes up with their own guidelines and the rules change every 10 or 15 kilometres. Some things should be agreed at a regional level.

“For motorways we need to have a national approach because the motorway network covers the whole country.”

Prime minister Rob Jetten said following last week’s deadly crash it was “unacceptable” for farm vehicles to be on motorways. “It leads to very dangerous situations,” he said.

World.title: Max Verstappen signs Red Bull extension on eve of Dutch GP
World.content:
Four-time Formula One world champion Max Verstappen has signed an extended contract with Red Bull Racing, ending speculation that he could leave the team or quit the sport altogether.

Verstappen, 28, was rumoured to be contemplating a move to rivals McLaren or Mercedes in recent months, but in a press release on Thursday he said he had chosen to stay with the team he saw as a “second family”.

”We have the best people and I’m excited to keep working together with everyone to get back to the top again,” he said. “This remains the ultimate goal that all of us have been working towards and will continue to pursue.”

He dismissed reports he had been in talks behind the scenes about a possible move to McLaren next season. “I was closer to quitting than changing teams,” he said.

The news that Verstappen will keep driving for Red Bull until 2030 will be welcomed by Dutch fans on the eve of the last edition of his home Grand Prix this weekend.

“To make this announcement during the last Grand Prix at Zandvoort is a great moment for me as well,” Verstappen said. “Hopefully we can give the fans a special send-off for the final race.”

Hybrid cars

Verstappen won the first three races after Zandvoort returned to the Formula One calendar in 2021, at a time when he dominated the sport, winning 71 races in 10 years and four consecutive world titles between 2021 and 2024.

This year he is standing sixth in the championship race, 110 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli, and is yet to record a win.

Verstappen has criticised the new hybrid cars introduced this season, that require drivers to save on fuel by recharging the battery during the race, describing them as “not fun to drive” and “anti-racing”.

Earlier this season he took part in the 24-hour race at the Nürburgring in Germany. Verstappen said being able to drive more endurance races in future years was “one of the factors and wishes” that influenced his decision to sign a new deal.

He was also caught up in the tensions within the Red Bull team surrounding the departure of former team boss Christian Horner, who left just over a year ago after being accused of sexually harassing a female colleague.

Horner was twice cleared of wrongdoing, but left with a £52 mln (€60 mln) payout amid accusations by Verstappen’s father, Jos, that he was “driving people apart”. Horner later said Max Verstappen played no role in his departure.

World.title: Prosecutors link three more deaths to drugs sold on internet
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch prosecutors say they have linked three more deaths to drugs bought on the Dutch-run Funcaps website, bringing the total number to 21.

Jord van W. and Stefan P., aged 31 and 30 and both from Limburg, have been charged with earning millions of euros from the sale of fake tranquilisers and sleeping pills, which are usually only available on prescription, as well as designer drugs.

The duo, who didn’t have a license to sell medicines, were closed down and sentenced in April by a Belgium court to three years in prison, including a year and a half suspended, for the illegal trafficking of medicines and drugs.

But they continued to trade in the Netherlands, where they achieved sales of €42 million in five years. They were arrested in August last year along with a third man, Van W.’s brother, who has been released but remains a suspect.

Prosecutors told a court in Zwolle that three more people had been identified who had died after taking drugs sold on Funcaps, while another two deaths are being investigated.

The website offered free gifts for large orders as well as a discount scheme and described its illegal medicines collection as “research chemicals”. They came with no usage information.

The website also sold sex toys, smoking tools and smart drugs, promising “discreet packaging” to clients.

“We did not foresee that a causal connection would be found in so many cases,” they said.

Many of the victims were “young people in the prime of their lives,” Zwolle judges heard. “That’s what makes this case so serious and unique.”

The next hearing is scheduled for November.

Coastal provinces could be hit by heavy rain, hail and even tornadoes on Thursday afternoon as the hot, dry summer weather in the Netherlands comes to an abrupt halt.

The meteorological institute KNMI has issued a code yellow warning for all coastal provinces, from Groningen to Zeeland, including the Wadden Islands.

The agency has warned people in the area to expect heavy showers, hail and gusts of up to 60 km/h. Tornadoes have already been spotted off the coast.

The warnings for hail and thunderstorms are in place until 5pm for Groningen and Friesland and until 6pm in other coastal areas, where tornadoes are forecast.

Heavy showers and storms are expected to continue through Friday, especially in the IJsselmeer region, with temperatures reaching 19 or 20 degrees in the daytime. Nights will be much cooler at between 10 and 14 degrees.

The best of the weekend weather will be on Sunday, with more sunshine and temperatures of up to 21 degrees.

World.title: Mortgages rise as first-time homebuyers take out more loans
World.content:
The number of mortgages taken out by Dutch homeowners in the first half of the year has gone up to €84.8 bn, with more first-time buyers getting on the ladder.

That was less than the record in the second half of 2025 but 8% higher than in the first half of 2025.

The latest figures show that more young people are taking out starter loans on top of their mortgages, which help them bridge the financial gap between the price of their home and the amount they are allowed to borrow as first-time buyers.

Loans were taken out on 8.3% of all starter home mortgages, up from 6.4% during the first half of 2025.

Starter loans, which are now offered to first-time buyers in more than 300 out of the 342 Dutch municipalities, proved especially popular with people up to the age of 25. Some 15% of this group obtained a starter loan in the first half of this year, compared to 8.6% of people between 25 and 35 years old.

The average amount borrowed was about € 37,000, up from €35,700 last year.

World.title: Three Dutch men killed in minibus crash during holiday in US
World.content:
Three Dutch nationals have died when a minibus collided with a tractor trailer in the US state of Ohio.

According to US media, the van carrying seven people was driven by Dutchman Gijs M. Odpam, 48, who apparently failed to yield at a stop sign in Knox County and was then struck by the tractor trailer.

Three men died at the scene of Tuesday’s collision: Arno Kramer, 55, Martijn E. Van Vooren, 44, and Hermanus J. Fortuin, 55.

The driver and three other passengers, all of whom were from the Netherlands, were taken to local hospitals. The extent of their injuries has not been disclosed.

The Dutch foreign ministry called the incident “a terrible accident” and sent staff from other regions in the US to Ohio to aid the victims and their families.

The Dutch nationals are said to be part of a travel group of 16 people who were divided between two vans. It’s unknown where the other van was at the time of the accident, which is still under investigation.

World.title: Gangs suspected of stealing fire station equipment for ram-raids
World.content:
More than 60 fire stations have been targeted in the last year by criminal gangs who steal hydraulic equipment to use in ram raids.

One fire station in Sassenheim, near Leiden in Zuid-Holland, was attacked three nights in a row in the last week, while 10 sites have been broken into across the country in the last fortnight.

Police told NRC the thieves were looking for equipment such as cutting gear and hydraulic jacks used to free people who are trapped beneath rubble.

The machines can be repurposed to break heavily fortified windows used by shops such as jewellers and electrical retailers. Last week thieves left behind a hydraulic spreader that they used to try to smash the window of a jewellery store in Den Bosch.

The number of break-ins has jumped in the last year, with just 18 thefts from fire stations recorded in 2025 and 17 the year before.

“We are trying to strengthen our response teams and making detecting these crimes a national priority,” police spokesman Dick Goijert said.

Safety boards would not say exactly what was taken in the most recent raids because the police investigation is ongoing and to avoid giving “unnecessary information to people with bad intentions”.

Accessibility issues

Fire station managers have tried to improve security, but locking away life-saving equipment means it takes longer to retrieve it in an emergency, when a few lost seconds can make the difference between life and death.

Evert Jansen, a former burglar who now works for the police to raise companies’ awareness of the need to improve security, said he suspected organised criminals were behind the thefts.

“Unless they know how the equipment works it’s difficult for them to use it,” Jansen told NRC. “Maybe the burglars are stealing it on the orders of experienced criminals.”

World.title: Community remembers 17-year-old Lisa, but safety concerns remain
World.content:
Exactly a year ago, 17-year-old Lisa was stabbed to death while cycling home to Abcoude after a night out in Amsterdam, sending shockwaves through the country and spearheading campaigns to combat violence against women.

Lisa’s body was found beside a cycleway in Duivendrecht, between the city and her home town, where she was pulled from her bike and stabbed to death while she was on the phone to police.

Shortly afterwards, a 22-year-old Nigerian man known as Christ Jude was arrested at a nearby Amsterdam refugee centre. Earlier this year, he confessed to killing Lisa, along with the rape and attempted rape of two other women in Amsterdam.

A memorial organised by a village church and youth centre will take place in Abcoude Thursday, where people can leave notes or light a candle for Lisa.

Family thanks

That community support, said Lisa’s family in a recent letter thanking Abcoude’s residents, has given them the “the security and strength to resume our lives step by step”.

“Not by hiding us, but by continuing with everything that was so dear to Lisa. Let’s laugh, dance, toast and celebrate life as Lisa did—full of dedication, with a generous smile and surrounded by friends,” they said.

Lisa’s murder took place during the Abcoude Festive Week (Feestweek Abcoude), a five-day annual festival that this year will be held from August 25-29. Organisers have consulted with Lisa’s family, and a commemorative event is expected to be included in the programme. The family’s letter thanking fellow villagers will also be distributed in the program’s booklet.

“It is almost unbelievable that it will soon be a year since Lisa passed away. Our world collapsed and the impact on the town was also immense,” reads the letter. “Thanks to all the villagers for the impressive minutes of silence we were able to experience together. Thank you for the hedge of honour you formed during the funeral, we will never forget these moments.”

Moving forward

Since the murder rattled the country and led to national soul-searching on how to protect women from violence, some things have changed.

Municipalities have taken to designing safer public spaces with women in mind, with several adding more lighting and pruning back shrubbery for more visibility.

But for Danique de Jong, it’s not enough. She organized a “We Claim the Night” crowd-funding campaign shortly after the murder that raised more than half a million euro in three days, money that has been spent on policy, education and victim assistance.

“Many of these measures are about reducing the feeling of insecurity: mowing bushes and setting up a lamp. Then we feel safer, but it doesn’t make us safer,” de Jong told RTV Utrecht. “If we only focus on pepper spray, pruning bunches and hanging lighting, nothing will change.”

Mostly at home

While she said she’s hopeful and applauds the changes, she calls for a cultural shift regarding violence against women. “4.5 million girls in the Netherlands had to deal with sexual violence before the age of 18…[with] someone in their environment who does not accept ‘no’”.

That’s because violence against women mostly occurs closer to home. “A girl being murdered by an unknown person or man is very disturbing but doesn’t happen very often,” Roos Koolhof, a healthcare psychologist who works with victims and those at risk of sexual assault for Levvel/Qpido, told Dutch News at the time of Lisa’s murder.

“Mostly assaults happen in a familiar atmosphere—86% of the time—by the neighbour or your stepfather or a boyfriend or a friend or someone they meet on social media.

“What happens more often is a slap on the ass or touching someone somewhere they don’t like,” she says. “And that is what we should talk about so it won’t happen anymore.”

A survey by the youth news program NOS Stories found that many women feel unsafe in certain places and often carry keys to protect themselves against attack.

Christ Jude’s trial is expected to start in Amsterdam in January.

A speed of 253 km/h (157 mph) has been reached by a Pendolino train during tests carried out as part of preparations to speed up rail connections between Poland’s major cities from next year. The plans will see the journey time between Warsaw and Kraków cut to well under two hours. “Polish rail is accelerating – and 250 km/h is just the beginning,” declared the infrastructure minister Dariusz Klimczak, alluding to plans for Poland to later begin running trains at speeds of up to 320 km/h. Osiągnęliśmy 250 km/h na Centralnej Magistrali Kolejowej❗🚅 Dzisiejsze nocne testy systemu GSM-R na linii nr 4 zakończyły się pełnym sukcesem. Oznacza to, że pociągi pojadą tą trasą z rozkładową prędkością 250 km/h już w przyszłym roku❗ Pozwoli to znacznie skrócić czas… pic.twitter.com/ndXvePZP4t — PLK SA (@PKP_PLK_SA) August 18, 2026 The tests on the GSM-R data transmission system, a communication standard designed to be used at very high speeds, were carried out on Monday night. Trains will be able to run on Poland’s Central Main Line (CMK), which connects Warsaw with Kraków and Katowice, at a scheduled speed of 250 km/h from December 2027. That will cut the expected journey time between Warsaw and Kraków, the country’s two largest cities, by around half an hour to 1 hour and 52 minutes, reports rail news service Portal Kolejowy. It will also be possible to travel from the capital to Wrocław, Poland’s third-largest city, in around three hours. The fastest current connection is 3 hours and 30 minutes. Reaching the target speed of 250 km/h was a “very important moment for Polish rail”, said Maciej Kaczorek, a board member of PKP Polskie Linie Kolejowe, the state railway infrastructure manager, quoted by news website Money.pl. Poland has been operating Pendolinos, built by France’s Alstom, since 2014. The trains are designed to run at speeds of up to 250 km/h, but currently operate at a maximum of 200 km/h in Poland and run on routes connecting Warsaw, Kraków, Wrocław and the Tricity area However, this week’s tests are not a record rail speed in Poland. In 2013, a Pendolino reached 293 km/h during a test on the CMK a year before the high-speed trains commenced passenger services in the country. A Polish Pendolino high-speed train has begun running in the Czech Republic for the first time. The Prague-Bohumín service will run until June as part of a certification process that Polish operator PKP Intercity hopes will lead to a Warsaw-Prague route https://t.co/hmUNd7ft0E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 10, 2026 Speaking to Rynek Kolejowy, deputy infrastructure minister Piotr Malepszak said that it had “taken too long” for the network to be adapted to allow regular speeds of 250 km/h. The current government, which took power in December 2023, has much broader plans for expanding high-speed rail travel in Poland, including building 2,700 km of tracks capable of carrying trains at 320 km/h. In December 2025, state rail operator PKP Intercity launched a tender for 20 such trains. They would cut the journey time between Warsaw and Gdańsk, on Poland’s Baltic coast, to around 100 minutes – from 2 hours 25 minutes currently – by 2040, Malepszak told the Polish Press Agency in June. Passenger numbers on Poland’s rail network have been booming in recent years. In the first half of 2026, a record 44.7 million passengers travelled with PKP Intercity, more than 10% up on the previous year’s record and some 45% higher than three years earlier. World.title: Polish government proposes middle-class tax cuts funded by increased rates for wealthiest
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has unveiled plans to reduce income tax rates for an estimated 3.5 million people earning around or slightly above average salaries. The costs of the cuts would be covered by increasing the tax rate for large companies and individuals with the highest earnings. The changes, which Prime Minister Donald Tusk says are intended to “provide relief and assistance to the growing middle class”, would come into effect from next year – when the government is facing re-election. However, the proposals still require approval from parliament, where Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, has a majority, and President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition and has vetoed a record number of bills. 📊 Nowa skala PIT będzie lepiej dopasowana do rosnących wynagrodzeń. Do 130 tys. zł pozostaje stawka 12%, między 130 a 150 tys. zł pojawi się 24%, a 32% zacznie obowiązywać dopiero powyżej 150 tys. zł. 💰 #WięcejWPortfelu pic.twitter.com/1S2MpSkVoC — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 19, 2026 The main elements of the proposed changes, which were outlined by Tusk and finance minister Andrzej Domański on Wednesday, are an increase in the earnings threshold at which the lowest rate of income tax is paid and the introduction of a new rate between the lowest and highest earnings brackets. Currently, there are two income tax brackets: the first taxes earnings of up to 120,000 zloty (around €27,800) at a rate of 12%; the second taxes earnings above that level at a rate of 32%. There is also a tax-free allowance for earnings of up to 30,000 zloty. Meanwhile, anyone who earns more than 1 million zloty a year pays an additional “solidarity levy” (effectively a third tax bracket) of 4% on income above that amount. Under the new proposals, the threshold for the first 12% tax bracket would be raised to 130,000 zloty. For earnings between 130,000 and 150,000 zloty, a new tax bracket of 24% would be introduced. Then earnings above 150,000 would be taxed at 32%. Tusk noted that, since his government took office, wages in Poland have increased by around 30%, bringing increasing numbers of people into the higher tax bracket. According to figures from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, in June this year, average monthly earnings at companies employing more than nine people were 9,401.58 zloty, the equivalent of almost 113,000 zloty a year. “We’re not talking about millionaires here; we’re talking about a growing middle class…on whose shoulders the financing of state security, defence spending, etc. rests to a large extent,” said Domański. “We want to change this…so that those who work hard to earn their average wage can clearly feel the relief,” added Tusk. “And we want this to be financed by the wealthiest companies and the wealthiest individuals, who have the lowest tax burden.” The number of ultra-wealthy individuals in Poland has more than doubled since 2021, a faster rate of growth than anywhere else in the world, according to a new study https://t.co/MNKgmjzn2U — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 Therefore, in order to finance the middle-class tax cuts, Tusk and Domański announced that the government would seek to increase corporate income tax from 19% to 22% for firms and tax capital groups that generate annual revenues above €50 million. Meanwhile, the solidarity levy for individuals earning over 1 million zloty a year would be increased by one percentage point, to 5%. “I am absolutely convinced that this will make our tax system more equitable,” declared Tusk. However, he also conceded that raising the income-tax-free amount from 30,000 to 60,000 zloty – as his Civic Platform (KO) party promised to do within its first 100 days in office – would not be possible for budgetary reasons, in particular the need to finance high defence spending. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) tax free. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build savings and channel money into the domestic financial market https://t.co/1xDHHJGYKX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 14, 2026 The prime minister said that the planned tax changes would be discussed further this week at a cabinet meeting devoted to next year’s state budget, which is currently being prepared. The relevant legislation will subsequently be submitted to parliament, with the aim of bringing it into force in 2027. However, Tusk acknowledged that there is a strong possibility of a veto by Nawrocki, who has blocked dozens of government bills, including fiscal measures. In December, Nawrocki vetoed an increase in the tax on alcoholic and sweet drinks. Last month, he effectively blocked a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits by sending it to the constitutional court for review. However, he did approve a law increasing the corporate income tax rate for banks. President @NawrockiKn has obstructed a planned windfall tax on fuel companies by sending it to the constitutional court, where it could stay for years The tax aimed to offset fuel price protection costs after the Iran war surgehttps://t.co/UojVuYhvdV — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 Next year’s budget will be closely watched given that Poland’s fiscal situation has become increasingly problematic in recent years. In 2024, the European Union placed Poland under its excessive deficit procedure, requiring Warsaw to commit to measures to bring down the deficit. However, last year the deficit actually rose, from 6.4% of GDP in 2024 to 7.3% in 2025, which was the second-highest level among all EU member states. This year, Poland’s public debt passed the EU’s limit of 60% of GDP for the first time on record. The situation has led two of the big three rating agencies, Fitch and Moody’s, to shift Poland’s credit outlook to negative. This year, Fitch warned that the political gridlock between Nawrocki and the government was making tackling the deficit and debt more difficult. Given that Poland will hold parliamentary elections in autumn 2027, it is unlikely that either the government or Nawrocki – who will be supporting the right-wing opposition – will be keen on any fiscal measures that either raise taxes or reduce spending in areas such as social policy and defence. Poland’s public debt has passed 60% of GDP for the first time, thereby exceeding the limit enshrined in EU law. Poland has launched a new advertising campaign to promote itself internationally and attract more tourists from “key European markets” and the United States. The new initiative, which has the slogan “Poland. More than you expected”, features global Polish icons such as football star Robert Lewandowski, supermodel Anja Rubik, and Hollywood filmmaker Jesse Eisenberg, who received Polish citizenship last year. A series of videos, the first of which was released Tuesday, will aim to present Poland as “modern, safe, diverse and authentic”, as well as “defying stereotypes”, says sports and tourism minister Jakub Rutnicki. Commissioned by his ministry and launched by the Polish Tourism Organisation (POT), the campaign will be conducted in Germany, Spain, Italy, the United Kingdom and the United States. The first video promotes Warsaw, Poland’s capital, and features Lewandowski, Rubik and Eisenberg appearing near the city’s landmarks. Polish actor Nikodem Rozbicki, meanwhile, plays the role of renowned 19th-century Polish composer Fryderyk Chopin. In the 30-second spot, Chopin’s character declares that Warsaw is “where my heart is” – a reference to the fact that Chopin’s heart, preserved in cognac, was brought back to the city from Paris by his sister shortly after his death in 1849 and is now immured in a pillar in the city’s Holy Cross Church. Lewandowski, who recently joined US football team Chicago Fire, tells viewers that Poland offers “more than you expected”, a reference to the campaign’s main slogan, which suggests to viewers that Poland may surprise them positively. “Research shows that people who have visited Poland rate it much more favourably than their previous perceptions or media reports suggested,” notes POT in its press release. Magdalena Krucz, the head of POT, adds that she believes the campaign “will be as surprising to audiences as Poland itself is to tourists who come to us for the first time”. However, the slogan is not new: it has been used by POT to promote Poland since 2021. The new campaign will also feature Nobel Peace Prize winner and former president Lech Wałęsa, who led the Solidarity movement that brought down Poland’s former communist regime. POT notes that he remains “one of the most recognisable symbols in the world of the fight for freedom and democracy”. The music is arranged by Radzimir Dębski, better known as Jimek, a Polish composer and conductor who has regularly performed with US rap legend Snoop Dogg. Polish-American NBA star @JeremySochan has joined a campaign to promote Poland as a tourist destination. His appearance has been received positively, but Sochan responded directly to one commentator who said a black person shouldn't be advertising Poland https://t.co/KXDok7IAXP — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 15, 2024 Poland has experienced a tourism boom in recent years. Last year, the country recorded the European Union’s second-fastest growth in the number of nights spent in tourist accommodation, behind only Malta. The biggest tourist draw is the historic city of Kraków, which was last year named the best city break destination in Europe by members of British consumer association and magazine Which? for the fifth time. This year, Time Out magazine rated Kraków the 16th best city in the world. However, the country has a wide range of tourist-friendly destinations, including long, sandy beaches on the northern Baltic coast, mountains in the south, the lake district of Masuria, as well as many historic cities and modern museums and galleries. Poland saw the EU's second-fastest growth in tourism in 2025, behind only the Mediterranean island state of Malta https://t.co/WVkRbHtU7o — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 19, 2026 The city of Lublin in eastern Poland, which will be a European City of Culture in 2029, last year welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors, including over half a million from abroad. The city is known for its rich Jewish history, and featured prominently in the 2024 Oscar-nominated film A Real Pain, directed by and starring Eisenberg, whose ancestors were Jews from Lublin and the nearby town of Krasnystaw. Last year, the sport and tourism ministry announced that it wants tourism to contribute 9% of GDP within a decade, from about 5% now. The strategy includes creating a “Polish brand” through which internationally recognised athletes, artists, historical figures and products are showcased more prominently. Last month, the government appointed a marketing and branding expert to develop a unified strategy for promoting the country abroad, saying the move will help boost tourism, support Polish products and attract foreign investment. The city of Lublin in eastern Poland welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors in 2025. World.title: Warsaw Uprising veteran and activist Wanda Traczyk-Stawska dies aged 99
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Wanda Traczyk-Stawska, a veteran of the Warsaw Uprising against Nazi-German occupation during World War Two, has died aged 99. Traczyk-Stawska, who survived imprisonment in German camps after the uprising, in her later years became a vocal advocate for the rights of women and disabled people. “Warsaw has lost someone extraordinary,” wrote Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, announcing her death on Wednesday. “A heroine, a soldier…but above all a teacher who, throughout her life, taught us what matters most: courage, dignity, and responsibility for our fellow human beings.” Odeszła Pani Wanda. Trudno w to uwierzyć. Warszawa straciła kogoś wyjątkowego – Bohaterkę, żołnierkę Powstania Warszawskiego, Honorową Obywatelkę miasta. Ale przede wszystkim nauczycielkę, która przez całe życie uczyła nas tego, co najważniejsze: odwagi, godności i… pic.twitter.com/uSNcsZ7c1P — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) August 19, 2026 Traczyk-Stawska, born in Warsaw in 1927, was only 12 years old when Nazi Germany invaded Poland. She initially became involved in the Grey Ranks (Szare Szeregi), an underground resistance movement associated with the Polish scouting movement, participating in sabotage operations. She later joined the Home Army (AK), Poland’s main resistance force, and, at the age of 17, served as a riflewoman and liaison during the Warsaw Uprising, taking the nom de guerre “Pączek” (meaning “Bud”). Traczyk-Stawska was seriously injured while fighting in the uprising. After the revolt was defeated, she was taken prisoner and subsequently held in various prisoner-of-war camps in Germany until the end of the war. After returning to Poland, Traczyk-Stawska earned a degree in psychology and began working as a teacher of disabled children in Warsaw. At the same time, she became an active figure in commemorating the uprising and its participants. In her final years, Traczyk-Stawska also became politically active. In 2018, she visited parliament to support a protest by disabled people and their carers, who were seeking more state support. Two years later, at the age of 93, she and another female uprising veteran, Hanna Stadnik, joined the mass Women’s Strike protests that broke out in response to the introduction of a near-total ban on abortion under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. “We women will not relent this time,” she told broadcaster TVN at the time. “In the uprising, we fought for our freedom, because there is no dignity without freedom. If we are currently treated like incubators, we have the right to fight for our dignity…We will fight – unarmed, but to the last woman – not to be treated like objects.” Traczyk-Stawska was also among a group of female Uprising veterans who that year criticised PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński for wearing, during a speech condemning the Women’s Strike protests, a badge featuring the anchor symbol that was used by the Home Army during the war. She was also an advocate for women’s rights more broadly. In 2023, in a speech at the 79th anniversary of the uprising, Traczyk-Stawska noted that, “at the beginning, the generals shouted: ‘Why do we need so many women?'” But, by the time the uprising ended, “we had been given the same rights as boys. And we won’t get rid of these rights. Because everyone, whether a man or a woman, is a citizen of this country and has equality written into the constitution”. Her speech then became overtly political, saying that “this [PiS] government needs to be completely changed, as it doesn’t remember that women have their own position enshrined in the constitution. That we are equal to men.” In both the 2020 and 2025 presidential elections, Traczyk-Stawska expressed support for the candidacy of Trzaskowski, who is a deputy leader of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party that is PiS’s main opponent. However, in both elections, Trzaskowski lost to PiS-backed candidates. Odeszła Wanda Traczyk-Stawska ps. „Pączek” – Bohaterka, Patriotka, wzór odwagi i niezłomności. Pokazywała, że prawdziwy patriotyzm to budowanie wspólnoty, empatia i otwartość na świat. Cześć Jej pamięci! 🕯️🤍 Najgłębsze wyrazy współczucia dla Bliskich. pic.twitter.com/nY0ijDSBlJ — Monika Sikora ⚡️ (@Moni_Sikora) August 19, 2026 Following news of Traczyk-Stawska’s death, many prominent figures paid tribute to her, in particular from the current KO-led ruling coalition. “Farewell, heroine,” wrote KO leader and Prime Minister Donald Tusk, sharing a photo of himself with Traczyk-Stawska and quoting one of her statements: “Do not stand, do not watch when evil happens, but react immediately, for that is your duty.” While she had fought against German occupation, Traczyk-Stawska later called for reconciliation. In her 2023 speech, she called Germany “our best neighbour” and said that the two countries must now “stand together”, including supporting Ukraine against Russian aggression. Today, Germany’s ambassador to Poland, Miguel Berger, expressed his “great sadness” at Traczyk-Stawska’s death, calling her an “advocate of dialogue in the process of Polish-German reconciliation and a passionate champion of peace, freedom, and human dignity”. „Nie stój, nie patrz, gdy się zło dzieje, tylko reaguj natychmiast, bo to jest twój obowiązek." – Wanda Traczyk-Stawska Żegnaj, Bohaterko. pic.twitter.com/MhfqlszVcI — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 19, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Main image credit: MSWiA (under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)

World.title: Poland “99% sure” fugitive opposition politician is in pro-Russian breakaway region of Moldova
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, says that they are “99% certain” that fugitive opposition politician Marcin Romanowski is in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links to Russia. Last week, judicial authorities in Poland confirmed that they had received a letter purportedly from Romanowski, who is wanted in Poland for 11 alleged crimes committed while he served as a deputy justice minister in the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. In the document, Romanowski claimed to be in Transnistria and requested safe passage back to Poland. However, as the authenticity of the letter had not been confirmed, some media outlets speculated that the politician may not, in fact, be in Transnistria. Meanwhile, the Moldovan authorities quickly announced that they had no record of Romanowski travelling to Transnistria, which is a landlocked territory that only has borders with Moldova and Ukraine and operates no commercial passenger flights. A former government minister who fled criminal charges in Poland appears to be in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links with Russia. Marcin Romanowski's whereabouts have been unknown since he left Hungary earlier this year https://t.co/MPWroFVbMe — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 13, 2026 Speaking on Tuesday morning, Przemysław Nowak, spokesman for Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office, said they have “still not confirmed” the veracity of Romanowski’s claim to be in Transnistria, reported broadcaster RMF. However, shortly afterwards, speaking ahead of a meeting of his cabinet on Tuesday, Tusk said he wanted to address the issue given there has been “a great deal of speculation and misinformation regarding Mr Romanowski and his whereabouts”. “I can say that the intelligence services of other countries in the region with which we cooperate have confirmed to us the information that Mr Romanowski is 99% certain – I say that just in case – to be in Transnistria, in Tiraspol,” he continued, referring to the capital of the breakaway region. "Pan Romanowski znajduje się na 99 procent w Naddniestrzu. Chyba nie trzeba tu komentarzy" Donald Tusk podczas posiedzenia rządu ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/muVQVKrOTs — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 18, 2026 Transnistria is a narrow strip of land in eastern Moldova that sought to become a separate state in the early 1990s as the Soviet Union collapsed, fighting a war between 1990 and 1992. Today, the territory, which has a population of around 360,000, operates as a de facto state but is not recognised by any other country. Its flag and national emblem feature the Soviet hammer and sickle. Transnistria has close ties with Russia, which maintains a military “peacekeeping” force there. Various experts and former intelligence officials have noted that it would be impossible for Romanowski to enter without Russia’s approval. The fact that Romanowski appears to be hiding there has led to criticism of PiS, the party Romanowski still technically serves as an MP and which publicly takes a strongly anti-Russian position. “If it is true that [Romanowski] is in Transnistria, a republic not recognised by anyone, de facto controlled 100% by Russia, then it must have happened through and with the participation of Russia,” said defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz last week. “Escaping under the Russian umbrella is the worst possible thing, because not only are they cowardly, but they are also joining the enemy of Poland,” he added. In his remarks today, Tusk said that Romanowski’s likely presence in Transnistria “speaks for itself regarding not only Mr Romanowski but the entire political group that covered up for and benefited from such people, and continues to cover up for them”. PiS politicians have largely avoided commenting, noting that it has not been confirmed that Romanowski is in Transnistria. However, deputy leader Przemysław Czarnek last week admitted that, if Romanowski did trael there, he would have “crossed a line”. Nie wyprzedzajmy faktów – powiedział poseł PiS Zbigniew Kuźmiuk, pytany, czy Marcin Romanowski może zostać zawieszony w partii.https://t.co/IQzuS8Ad7O — tvn24 (@tvn24) August 14, 2026 Romanowski served as a deputy justice minister in the former PiS government from 2019 until 2023, when the party lost power to a new ruling coalition led by Tusk. In 2024, prosecutors announced that they wanted to charge him with 11 crimes, including participating in an organised criminal group and using crime as a source of income. However, he instead fled to Hungary, where he was granted asylum by the then-government of Viktor Orbán, a PiS ally. When Orbán lost power earlier this year, his successor, Péter Magyar, promised to extradite both Romanowski and Zbigniew Ziobro, the former PiS justice minister who had also fled criminal charges in Poland and been granted asylum by Orbán. However, as Magyar was sworn in as the new prime minister, Ziobro fled to the United States, where he remains, and Romanowski disappeared, leading to months of speculation as to his whereabouts. Both politicians deny the accusations against them and claim to be victims of political persecution by Tusk’s government. Poland has formally asked the US to detain and extradite former justice minister @ZiobroPL, who faces multiple criminal charges. He denies wrongdoing and calls the case political revengehttps://t.co/BXdQgWm61q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 In his comments on Tuesday morning, Nowak said that prosecutors had found “no grounds whatsoever” to approve Romanowski’s request for safe passage to Poland. He noted that “the suspect has evaded legal proceedings, questioned the legality of the authorities’ actions, left Poland and then Hungary to avoid arrest, and publicly declared his lack of intention to return to the country due to the ongoing criminal proceedings against him”. Polish prosecutors are still, however, attempting to confirm Romanowski’s whereabouts and secure his extradition to Poland to face justice. He is subject to a European Arrest Warrant. However, that applies only in EU countries, and Moldova is not a member of the bloc. World.title: FedEx-led €7.8bn takeover of Polish delivery giant InPost wins EU approval
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The European Commission has granted approval for a consortium led by American transportation conglomerate FedEx to take over Polish delivery giant InPost in a deal worth €7.8 billion (33.7 billion zloty). InPost, which operates in France, Spain, the UK, Portugal, Italy and the Benelux countries, as well as in its home market, confirmed on Tuesday that it had received the green light from the EU for the deal, which was announced in February. If it goes through, the takeover will see a consortium made up of FedEx along with existing InPost investors, Advent, A&R, and PPF, purchase all of the company’s shares at a price of €15.60 each. Konsorcjum inwestorów, w którym jednym z uczestników jest amerykański @FedEx, uzyskało bezwarunkową zgodę KE na nabycie wszystkich akcji @InPostPL @RBrzoska https://t.co/F4AleTCViO — WNP.PL (@wnppl) August 18, 2026 The group behind the deal says the aim is to help InPost continue its recent rapid expansion. The firm will retain its name, branding and Polish headquarters. Founder and CEO Rafał Brzoska will remain in place, as well as being a major shareholder through A&R, which is his investment vehicle. The deal will see Advent, an American private equity firm, and FedEx each hold 37% of InPost. A&R would have 16% and PPF, a Czech investment fund founded by the late billionaire Petr Kellner, 10%. Currently, PPF holds 28.75%, A&R 12.49%, and Advent 6.5%. The initial offer period for the consortium’s takeover was due to end on 27 July. However, on 22 July, it was extended until 18 September due to the fact that antitrust proceedings in the EU and Vietnam were still ongoing. In its announcement today of EU approval, InPost noted that it is still awaiting a green light from the Vietnam Competition Commission but expects a decision to be made by 8 September. Although the Polish company has no operations in Vietnam, FedEx has been present on the market since 1994. InPost has grown rapidly in recent years through its pioneering use of parcel lockers, first in Poland and then across western Europe. In the UK, it has established a network of over 14,000 parcel lockers, including in branches of the British Post Office. In June this year, French President Emannuel Macron thanked InPost for its latest investment in France, where the firm – which operates there through its subsidiary Mondial Relay – is planning to spend a further €500 million to expand its presence. In the first quarter of 2026, InPost saw its revenue rise 31% year-on-year to reach 3.9 billion zloty. That included 121% growth in the UK, 28% in the Eurozone and 9% in Poland itself. However, the group’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA), a measure of profitability of business operations, were down 4% to 902 million zloty. World.title: Twelve killed as Polish coach crashes in Hungary
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Twelve people have died after a bus carrying Polish pilgrims from Medjugorje in Bosnia and Herzegovina back to Poland crashed on a motorway in Hungary. Initial findings indicate that the cause of the accident was the driver of the coach falling asleep. Political leaders in both Poland and Hungary have offered condolences to the families of the victims, while the Polish foreign ministry has set up a special helpline for those affected. BREAKING: 12 people have been killed after a Polish tourist bus crashed on a motorway in Hungary https://t.co/PAiZ4D1jU3 📺 Sky 501, Virgin 602, Freeview 233 and YouTube pic.twitter.com/yxW9tBN5bw — Sky News (@SkyNews) August 16, 2026 The accident occurred at around 1 a.m. local time on the night of Saturday to Sunday on the M3 motorway in Hungary. Later on Sunday morning, Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar confirmed that 12 people had died and at least 10 were seriously injured. According to information from the Hungarian emergency services, 57 passengers and two drivers had been on the bus. “The driver probably fell asleep at the wheel”, resulting in the vehicle veering off the road and into a ditch, said police in a statement quoted by Polsat News. Polsat reports that the group is from around Strzyżów, a town in southeastern Poland. The owner of the local company that had been transporting them told Business Insider Polska that the coach “was driven by two experienced drivers”. Twelve people lost their lives and at least ten were seriously injured overnight when a bus carrying Polish tourists overturned and went off the road into a ditch on the M3 motorway. My sincere condolences to the families of the victims. I am grateful to all those who took part… — Magyar Péter (Ne féljetek) (@magyarpeterMP) August 16, 2026 Polish media outlets reported that the group in the bus were pilgrims on their way back to Poland from Medjugorje, which is a popular destination for Catholic pilgrimages due to a series of reported visions of the Virgin Mary that have occurred there. Polish foreign ministry spokesman Maciej Wewiór later confirmed to broadcaster TVN that “everything indicates they were returning from Medjugorje”. The authorities in Podkarpackie, the province of Poland where the group was from, also reported that they were pilgrims returning from Bosnia and Herzegovina. The accident on Sunday morning took place just after the end of celebrations of the Assumption of Mary on Saturday, which had included the unveiling in Poland of Europe’s tallest statue of Mary. Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki, issued a statement on Sunday morning expressing his “deep sorrow…in the face of this unimaginable tragedy” and offering “prayer and profound compassion for the families and loved ones of the victims”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk likewise expressed his “deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims” and thanked the Hungarian emergency services for undertaking the rescue operation. Andrii Sybiha, the foreign minister of Ukraine, which borders both Poland and Hungary, also offered his “heartfelt condolences” and said that “Ukraine stands in solidarity with the friendly Polish people and shares their grief”. The Polish embassy in Budapest has set up a special helpline for family members and loved ones of those involved in the crash. World.title: Europe’s biggest Virgin Mary statue – taller than Rio’s Christ the Redeemer – unveiled in Polish village
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The tallest statue of the Virgin Mary in Europe has been officially opened in the small village of Konotopie in central Poland. Towering over the rural landscape at 55.6 metres high, the monument, whose construction was funded by a wealthy local couple, is taller than the famous Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The new landmark, which is also the tallest religious statue of any kind in Europe, was unveiled on 15 August, when Catholics celebrate the assumption of Mary into heaven. The consecration ceremony was led by Krzysztof Wętkowski, bishop of the diocese of Włocławek in which Konotopie, which has a population of only around 130 people, is located. The local community hopes that the statue will become a major site of pilgrimage. Among those to attend the ceremony was former Polish president and Nobel Peace Prize winner Lech Wałęsa. “We sinners ask Our Lady of Mercy to take care of the whole nation,” wrote the 82-year-old in a post on social media, sharing photos of himself at the statue. Construction of the concrete statue took 18 months and reportedly cost around 100 million zloty (€23.2 million). Those costs were covered by the couple behind the project, Roman and Grażyna Karkosik. After making his fortune investing in undervalued companies during Poland’s post-communist transition in the 1990s, Roman Karkosik had by the early 21st century become one of Poland’s richest people, though his fortune has since diminished somewhat, according to estimates. The couple – who keep an extremely low profile, rarely giving interviews and never speaking publicly about the project to build the statue of Mary – live in a restored 18th-century palace around 2 kilometres away, from where they can see the new monument. Konotopie’s statue of Mary has now overtaken one in Miribel, France, as Europe’s tallest. But it is still some distance behind the tallest in the world, the 98-metre Mother of All Asia–Tower of Peace in Batangas City, Philippines. Until recently, Poland also had the tallest statue of Jesus in the world, the 33-metre-high Jesus Christ the King of the Universe monument, erected in the town of Świebodzin in 2010. However, in 2024, it was overtaken by a 61-metre-tall statue of Jesus in Indonesia. The design for the statue of Mary in Konotopie was originally conceived in the form of a two-metre-high model by sculptor Adam Jakub Matejkowski, who told the Polish edition of Forbes magazine that the Karkosiks had specifically requested that the statue be larger than Świebodzin’s Christ. Chief engineer Bartłomiej Niesłuchowski told broadcaster TVN that it took months to find a company willing and able to undertake such a project. Because no suppliers in Poland could produce the material needed for the unique mould into which the concrete would be poured, it had to be manufactured in Italy. The monument will be free for the public to access, including its observation deck, located 15 metres up on the pedestal upon which Mary stands. The site is expected to become a place of pilgrimage, with local authorities preparing for an influx of people. “We’re already seeing growing interest in investment plots, including restaurants,” Renata Gołębiewska, mayor of the nearby town of Kikoł, told the Rzeczpospolita daily. “But it’s too early to assess the impact.” Poland is one of Europe’s most religious countries. Just over 70% of the population identify as Catholic, according to the most recent national census, while around 30% attend Sunday mass. However, religiosity has been falling rapidly in recent years, especially among young Poles. The Catholic church in Poland has also been hit by a series of scandals relating to historical child sex abuse as well as accusations that it interferes in politics. The proportion of Catholics who attend Sunday mass in Poland has stabilised at around 30% after falling from a peak of 57%, new church data show.
